title: Jigsaw Initiative: Adaptive small-tail prefetch + quant validation pipeline
creator: Sofia Gomez
description:
Problem: token unit economics are dominated by a long tail of low-value, latency-sensitive requests. Current one-size quant profiles and generic prefetch/batching heuristics produce either unacceptable quality regressions or limited savings.

Objective: build a repeatable pipeline that evaluates combinations of adaptive small-tail prefetch heuristics and per-segment quantization profiles against representative workloads so we can: 
1) Identify safe quant profiles that yield >15% token cost reduction with <=1% regression on critical eval sets;
2) Deploy adaptive prefetch rules that reduce redundant KV growth for short-context requests and improve batching efficiency for microbursts;
3) Automate canary validation and rollback criteria so production rollouts are safe across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope: experimentation harness, dataset curation (short-context + mixed-length tails), evaluation metrics, ops runbook, canary and rollback gates, dashboarding for unit economics and quality. Excludes core kernel changes and hardware procurement decisions (those stay with serving/runtime eng teams).

Artifacts: PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Jigsaw+Initiative+PRD, Experiment spec: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/jigsaw-experiments, Sandbox dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/jigsaw-sandbox, Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/jigsaw-proto/pull/12

Success metric: measurable, repeatable token-econ improvement with no regressions above the acceptance criteria and an operational playbook that can be executed by Platform and Solutions teams.
progress_updates: 2025-11-16: Kickoff meeting with Eng(runtime), Eng(infra), Design, SRE. Aligned on dataset boundaries and short-context definition (<128 tokens). Action: Eng to produce sampled traces by 2025-11-22.

2025-11-22: Eng produced workloads from hosted fleet and dedicated testbeds. Initial samples show 27% of requests are <=64 tokens but account for only 8% of token volume. Hypothesis: optimizing small-tail offers disproportionate latency-cost wins.

2025-11-28: Draft experiment grid reviewed. Decided to run closed-loop validation on 3 quant profiles and 4 prefetch heuristics. Design provided structured output templates for quality checks. Security asked for a minimal data retention plan — privacy review scheduled.

2025-11-30: First sandbox run completed. Cost signal shows 12% token reduction with aggressive quant, but hallucination checks flagged 1.9% regression on the safety eval set. Team to add fallback gating and per-endpoint opt-outs.
2025-12-02: Product review with VP. Approved phase-gate for canary if regression <=1% and p95 latency delta <= 10ms. Eng to implement canary rollback automation and telemetry tagging by 2025-12-15.
2025-12-03: Design review completed for rollout banners and console UX for opt-outs. Next: field trial in dedicated pool with 5% traffic for 2 weeks.
acceptance_criteria: Automated pipeline that runs experiment grid end-to-end against canonical workloads
Quant profiles that demonstrate >=15% token-unit cost reduction on at least 2 representative workloads with <=1% regression on labeled eval sets
Adaptive prefetch rules that reduce KV growth for short-context requests by >=20% in sandbox metrics
Canary automation that forces rollback when quality or latency gates are exceeded
Console views showing per-route cost delta, p50/p95 latency, and a quality-signal time series for trialed routes
Runbook and handoff docs for Platform and Solutions teams to operationalize rollouts
